semester: 4th semester (winter semester start); 5th semester (summer semester start)

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to work in a project group on a constructive project for the development of a self-contained, moderately complex mechanical technical structure with accompanying coaching.
They can organize themselves in a team and jointly formulate, maintain, and consider technical boundary conditions (requirements list, specifications) as well as a schedule.

They understand the basic physical phenomena and can use balances on elementary-geometric equivalent models to access the force, motion, power, and stress quantities within the technical structure and individual components.

They can independently use relevant components from Machine Elements 1 and 2, possibly 3, and the associated calculation methods for concrete self-designed problems, considering sustainability aspects such as material utilization, reduction of processing, waste avoidance wherever possible in conception and design.
They can document and reflect on the solution path and result graphically and textually.
They have experience with conflicting goals and the iterative design process characterized by designing and discarding.

syllabus_topics: Design (principled sketching, designing, evaluating, discarding, varying, deciding....) of a self-contained mechanical structure according to specifications and schedule.
Model building and calculations according to Technical Mechanics and Machine Elements 1 + 2 (3)
Creation of a meaningful, comprehensible, and structured documentation of the process and result, as well as a reflection on one's own teamwork and the solution.
Graphic representations according to drawing standards by hand and/or with CAD, in parts standard-compliant manufacturing documents, parts lists, assembly instructions.
teaching_methods: Coached project work in small groups
Introductory sessions for the full course (if applicable)
Topic-centered events with participants from multiple groups (if applicable)
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The weighting of the grade for the final grade is based on the credit points.
